"""Conservative Go resolution over every ``.go`` file of one capture (docs/go.md).

A package is the files of one directory sharing a package clause, keyed
``module:go:<dir>/<package>`` (``module:go:<package>`` at the root). The ``module``
line of each captured ``go.mod`` maps import paths to directories; anything else
(the standard library, other modules, ``replace``, ``go.work``, vendoring) stays
unresolved. Build constraints are not evaluated: same-named declarations in
platform files make a reference ambiguous rather than choosing one.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

from oxide.core.languages.go import Parsed
from oxide.core.languages.python import Use
from oxide.core.languages.python_resolve import Edge, Res, edge_target, structural
from oxide.models import Entity, RelationKind, SourceRef

_MODULE = re.compile(rb"^\s*module\s+\"?([^\s\"]+?)\"?\s*(?://.*)?$", re.MULTILINE)
_TESTS = ("Test", "Benchmark", "Fuzz", "Example")

type Package = tuple[str, str]  # (directory, package clause)
type Site = tuple[int, int]  # (file, scope)


def module_key(package: Package) -> str:
    directory, name = package
    return f"module:go:{directory}/{name}" if directory else f"module:go:{name}"


def is_test(path: str, name: str) -> bool:
    """``go test`` discovery: Test, Benchmark, Fuzz and Example functions of a _test.go
    file, whose suffix does not start with a lower-case letter."""
    if not path.endswith("_test.go"):
        return False
    for prefix in _TESTS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            rest = name[len(prefix) :]
            return not rest or not rest[0].islower()
    return False


def _exported(name: str) -> bool:
    return name[:1].isupper()


def symbol_keys(path: str, parsed: Parsed) -> list[str]:
    """The file key, then ``symbol:<path>#<segment>`` per scope: the name, or
    ``Owner.Name`` for methods. Equal segments (``init``, platform duplicates, broken
    code) take ``~n`` in source order, so keys are unique within the file."""
    decls = [s.decl for s in parsed.scopes[1:] if s.decl is not None]
    segments = [f"{d.owner}.{d.name}" if d.owner else d.name for d in decls]
    named = [""] * len(decls)
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    for j in sorted(range(len(decls)), key=lambda j: decls[j].start):
        n = seen.get(segments[j], 0)
        seen[segments[j]] = n + 1
        named[j] = segments[j] + (f"~{n}" if n else "")
    return [f"file:{path}", *(f"symbol:{path}#{s}" for s in named)]


@dataclass(slots=True)
class _File:
    path: str
    digest: str
    parsed: Parsed
    keys: list[str]
    package: Package
    test: bool  # a _test.go file: visible only to test files of its own package


class Resolver:
    def __init__(self, files: list[tuple[str, str, Parsed]], mods: dict[str, bytes]) -> None:
        self.roots: dict[str, str] = {}  # directory of a go.mod -> its module path
        for path, data in mods.items():
            found = _MODULE.search(data)
            if found is not None:
                self.roots[path.rpartition("/")[0]] = found.group(1).decode("utf-8", "replace")
        self.files: list[_File] = []
        self.packages: dict[Package, list[int]] = {}
        # Per package: package-level names, and methods by (receiver type, name).
        self.tops: dict[Package, dict[str, list[Site]]] = {}
        self.methods: dict[Package, dict[tuple[str, str], list[Site]]] = {}
        self.tests: set[str] = set()
        self.call_targets: set[str] = set()
        for path, digest, parsed in files:
            directory = path.rpartition("/")[0]
            package = (directory, parsed.package) if parsed.package else (path, "")
            i, keys = len(self.files), symbol_keys(path, parsed)
            self.files.append(_File(path, digest, parsed, keys, package, path.endswith("_test.go")))
            self.packages.setdefault(package, []).append(i)
            tops = self.tops.setdefault(package, {})
            methods = self.methods.setdefault(package, {})
            for k, s in enumerate(parsed.scopes):
                if s.parent != 0 or s.decl is None:
                    continue
                if s.decl.kind != "method":
                    tops.setdefault(s.decl.name, []).append((i, k))
                    if s.decl.kind in ("function", "struct", "interface", "type"):
                        self.call_targets.add(keys[k])
                    if s.decl.kind == "function" and is_test(path, s.decl.name):
                        self.tests.add(keys[k])
                elif s.decl.owner:
                    self.call_targets.add(keys[k])
                    methods.setdefault((s.decl.owner, s.decl.name), []).append((i, k))

    def _visible(self, sites: list[Site], test: bool) -> list[str]:
        return sorted(self.files[i].keys[k] for i, k in sites if test or not self.files[i].test)

    def _top(self, package: Package, name: str, test: bool) -> list[str]:
        return self._visible(self.tops[package].get(name, []), test)

    def _lookup(self, i: int, k: int, name: str, imports: dict[str, list[Package]]) -> Res:
        """Candidates for ``name`` or ``q.name`` used in scope ``k`` of file ``i``."""
        file = self.files[i]
        scope = file.parsed.scopes[k]
        qualifier, _, member = name.rpartition(".")
        if not qualifier:
            if name in scope.bound or name == scope.receiver:
                return None
            found = self._top(file.package, name, file.test)
            if not found and _exported(name):  # dot imports cannot redeclare package names
                found = sorted(x for p in imports.get(".", []) for x in self._top(p, name, False))
            return found or None
        if qualifier in scope.bound:
            return None
        if qualifier == scope.receiver and scope.decl is not None and scope.decl.owner:
            sites = self.methods[file.package].get((scope.decl.owner, member), [])
            return self._visible(sites, file.test) or None  # promoted methods: unresolved
        if qualifier in imports and _exported(member):
            return (
                sorted(x for p in imports[qualifier] for x in self._top(p, member, False)) or None
            )
        return None

    def _owner(self, directory: str) -> str | None:
        """The directory of the nearest go.mod at or above ``directory``."""
        while directory not in self.roots:
            if not directory:
                return None
            directory = directory.rpartition("/")[0]
        return directory

    def _directory(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        """The captured directory of an import path, through the longest module path."""
        roots = [r for r, m in self.roots.items() if path == m or path.startswith(m + "/")]
        longest = max((len(self.roots[r]) for r in roots), default=0)
        roots = [r for r in roots if len(self.roots[r]) == longest]
        if len(roots) != 1:
            return None
        rest = [p for p in path[longest:].split("/") if p]
        if any(p in ("testdata", "vendor") or p[0] in "._" for p in rest):
            return None  # directories the go tool ignores; vendoring is unmodeled
        directory = "/".join(p for p in (roots[0], *rest) if p)
        return directory if self._owner(directory) == roots[0] else None

    def _imported(self, path: str) -> list[Package]:
        """Importable packages of the import path's directory: not ``main`` or an
        external test package, and with a non-test file. More than one is ambiguous."""
        directory = self._directory(path)
        if directory is None:
            return []
        return sorted(
            p
            for p, members in self.packages.items()
            if p[0] == directory
            and p[1] not in ("", "main")
            and not p[1].endswith("_test")
            and any(not self.files[i].test for i in members)
        )

    def derive(self, entities: list[Entity], edges: list[Edge]) -> None:
        for package in sorted(p for p in self.packages if p[1]):
            directory, name = package
            label, owner = directory or ".", self._owner(directory)
            if owner is not None:  # the import path
                rest = directory[len(owner) :].strip("/")
                label = "/".join(p for p in (self.roots[owner], rest) if p)
            label += "_test" if name.endswith("_test") else ""
            key = module_key(package)
            entities.append(Entity(key, "module", "module", label, None, None, False))
            edges.append(structural("contains", "repo", key, None))
            for i in self.packages[package]:
                file_key = f"file:{self.files[i].path}"
                edges.append(structural("contains_logical", key, file_key, None))
        for i in range(len(self.files)):
            self._emit(i, entities, edges)

    def _emit(self, i: int, entities: list[Entity], edges: list[Edge]) -> None:
        file = self.files[i]

        def evidence(start: int, end: int) -> SourceRef:
            return SourceRef(file.path, start, end, file.digest)

        def edge(kind: RelationKind, source: str, res: Res, use: Use) -> Edge:
            targets, resolution, basis = edge_target(res, kind == "calls")
            shown = None if resolution == "resolved" else use.name
            at = evidence(use.start, use.end)
            return Edge(kind, source, targets, resolution, basis, shown, at)

        imports: dict[str, list[Package]] = {}
        for item in file.parsed.imports:
            found = self._imported(item.path)
            use = Use(item.path, item.start, item.end)
            edges.append(edge("imports", file.keys[0], [module_key(p) for p in found] or None, use))
            for p in found if item.alias != "_" else []:
                imports.setdefault(item.alias or p[1], []).append(p)

        for k, scope in enumerate(file.parsed.scopes):
            key = file.keys[k]
            if scope.decl is not None and scope.parent is not None:
                d = scope.decl
                source = evidence(d.start, d.end)
                test = key in self.tests
                entities.append(Entity(key, "symbol", d.kind, d.name, d.signature, source, test))
                edges.append(structural("contains", file.keys[scope.parent], key, None))
                if scope.parent == 0 and file.package[1]:
                    edges.append(structural("defines", module_key(file.package), key, source))
                if scope.parent == 0 and d.kind == "method" and d.owner:
                    res = self._lookup(i, 0, d.owner, imports)
                    edges.append(edge("references", key, res, Use(d.owner, d.start, d.end)))
            for ref in scope.refs:
                edges.append(edge("references", key, self._lookup(i, k, ref.name, imports), ref))
            for call in scope.calls:
                targets = self._lookup(i, k, call.name, imports)
                if targets is not None:
                    targets = [
                        candidate for candidate in targets if candidate in self.call_targets
                    ] or None
                relation = edge("calls", key, targets, call)
                callee = relation.targets[0] if relation.resolution == "resolved" else None
                if key in self.tests and callee and callee not in self.tests:
                    at = evidence(call.start, call.end)
                    edges.append(
                        Edge("tested_by", callee, (key,), "resolved", "heuristic", None, at)
                    )
                edges.append(relation)
# Go source support

`oxide-go-v1` adds Go as a language slice of the existing engine: `core/languages/go.py`
extracts syntax facts with `tree-sitter-go==0.25.0`, `core/languages/go_resolve.py` resolves
them over the whole capture. No Go toolchain, `go list`, `gopls`, module download
or repository code runs during indexing or querying. The ordinary Python API, CLI,
retrieval, graph, router and context packer serve these files unchanged, and MCP
remains exactly one tool, `oxide_search`, with `search` and `context` modes.

## Extraction and identity

`.go` files report `FileInfo.language == "go"`. Package-level declarations become
symbols:

| Go declaration | Kind | Key segment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `func F` (generic or not, with or without a body) | `function` | `F` |
| `func (r *T) M` / `func (T[P]) M` | `method` | `T.M` |
| `type S struct` | `struct` | `S` |
| `type I interface` | `interface` | `I` |
| method element `M()` of an interface `I` | `method`, nested in `I` | `I.M` |
| any other `type T U` or alias `type T = U` | `type` | `T` |
| each name of a package-level `const` / `var` | `constant` / `variable` | the name |

Keys are `symbol:<path>#<segment>`. Methods keep the file as their physical parent,
so their segment names the receiver base type (pointer, type arguments and
parentheses stripped). Equal segments in one file (several `init` functions,
declarations that differ only by build tags, broken code) take `~n` in source order.
Blank (`_`) declarations and declarations inside function bodies are not symbols;
their code stays in the enclosing symbol. Entity names are the plain identifiers
(`Get`, not `T.Get`).

A grouped declaration's entries (`const ( … )`, `var ( … )`, `type ( … )`) get their
own spec's byte range; a single declaration spans the whole declaration, keyword
included. Several names of one spec (`var a, b = f(), g()`) share its range.
Signatures are the declaration header up to the body (`func (s *Store) Get(key Key)
(string, bool)`, `type Store struct`, `const ModeRead = 1`). Doc comments are not
part of a symbol's range.

A package is the `.go` files of one directory that share a package clause:
`module:go:<dir>/<package>`, or `module:go:<package>` for the repository root.
Files of an external test package (`package foo_test`) and of a second clause in the
same directory are separate modules. A module's name is its import path when a
captured `go.mod` owns the directory (`example.com/shop/store`, `…/store_test`),
otherwise the directory. Modules `contain_logical` their files and `define` their
package-level symbols. Interface method elements are contained by their interface.

`go test` discovery marks `TestXxx`, `BenchmarkXxx`, `FuzzXxx` and `ExampleXxx`
package-level functions of `_test.go` files as tests (the suffix must not start with
a lower-case letter, so `Testable` is not a test). A resolved call made inside a test,
including inside its closures such as `t.Run` bodies, adds `tested_by`, the same
heuristic as the Python and TypeScript slices.

## Resolution

Everything below is established syntactically and by the Go specification's
package and file scoping. Nothing needs a type checker, and nothing that would is
inferred.

- **Imports.** The `module` line of every captured `go.mod` maps an import path to a
  directory by the longest matching module path. The directory's nearest `go.mod`
  must be that module (a nested module owns its subtree). The importable packages
  are that directory's package clauses other than `main` and `_test` packages, with
  at least one non-test file; one is resolved, several ambiguous. Paths through
  `testdata`, `vendor`, or `.`/`_`-prefixed directories, the standard library and
  other modules are unresolved and keep the path as their name.
- **Package scope.** A bare name resolves to package-level declarations of the
  same package in any of its files. Declarations in `_test.go` files are visible
  only from test files of the same package. An exported name not declared in the
  package can come from a dot-imported local package.
- **Qualified names.** `pkg.Name` resolves through the file's import binding: an
  alias, or the target's package clause (not the last path element). Only exported
  names of non-test files are visible.
- **Receivers.** Inside a method, `r.M()` on the receiver `r` resolves to the
  method `M` declared with the same receiver base type in the same package.
- **Conservative locals.** A name bound anywhere in a declaration (parameters,
  results, type parameters, `:=`, local `var`/`const`/`type`, `range`, type switch
  and `select` bindings, function literal parameters) is opaque throughout that
  declaration, so shadowing never produces a wrong edge. A receiver bound again is
  an ordinary local.
- **Calls** cover calls through an identifier or `x.F`, explicit instantiations
  (`F[T](x)`, `pkg.F[T](x)`), and conversions `T(x)` (resolved to the type).
- **References** cover a method's receiver type, embedded struct fields and
  interface elements, composite literal types (`T{}`, `&pkg.T{}`), and type
  names in those supported type positions. Generic instantiation arguments are not
  emitted as separate references; Go's grammar does not distinguish all of them from
  indexed expressions without type information.

Same-named declarations in several files (typically `_linux.go` / `_windows.go` or
`//go:build` variants) make a reference ambiguous, listing every candidate:
build constraints and `GOOS`/`GOARCH` file suffixes are not evaluated.

## Not modeled

These need type information, a build configuration or the module graph, and stay
unresolved (with their name) or absent rather than guessed:

- method calls on anything but the receiver (`v.M()`, `pkg.Var.M()`, chained
  calls), promoted methods and fields through embedding, interface dispatch and
  implementations (there is no `implements` relation);
- method values and expressions (`T.M`, `(*T).M`), and calls of function values
  or struct fields;
- uses that are not calls or the type references above: values of constants,
  variables and functions (`return ErrClosed`, `f := New`), and types in
  signatures, fields, and composite element types (`[]T{}`, `map[K]V{}`);
- the standard library, third-party modules, `replace` and `go.work` directives,
  vendored packages, cgo (`import "C"`) and generated code that is not captured;
- build constraints, file name `GOOS`/`GOARCH` suffixes and `ignore` builds;
- block scoping (a shadowed name is opaque in the whole declaration), labels,
  `goto`, and local types and functions as symbols;
- struct fields as symbols, and the type-checked validity of the program.

Structural search (`Repository.structural_search`, ast-grep) remains Python and
TypeScript only.

## Reliability

The shared bounded native query, downward-only node reads, depth limit (65,535),
UTF-8 check and bounded syntax diagnostics apply unchanged. Invalid UTF-8 or
excessive depth is unsupported file evidence; grammar recovery is partial and keeps
recovered declarations. `go.mod` files stay unsupported file evidence and are read
only for their `module` line during resolution, which always reruns over the full
capture, so a `go.mod`-only change re-resolves correctly with all facts reused.

Facts are cached by `(go, source digest)` under `oxide-go-facts-v1`; the cache decoder
validates types, ranges, identifier names, the package clause and the scope tree,
and anything else is parsed again. Derivation components add `go` (`oxide-go-v1`)
and `go-parser`; older indices are re-indexed. Evidence and reproduction:
[phase-6/go-v1](phase-6/go-v1/README.md).

commit 738741b374f003bfa8227459e1d0ac085e5e31e1
Author: Kiy-K <tannguyenkhoitruong@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 30 18:41:47 2026 +0700

    feat: Java language slice (tree-sitter-java) with javac-verified resolution
    
    - java.py extracts syntax facts (types, members, annotation elements,
      imports, calls, references, scoped bindings) with one compiled
      tree-sitter-java 0.23.5 query; java_facts.py holds the facts' cache
      codec; java_resolve.py resolves packages, imports, javac type-lookup
      order, inherited members and arity-filtered calls conservatively.
    - Declaration headers resolve as javac does: annotations, type-parameter
      bounds, extends/implements and permits look up in the enclosing scope
      (own type parameters stay visible; record components see members).
      Measured with javac 25 probes in docs/phase-6/java-v1/verification.
    - gson javac oracle: 14,671 agree / 0 disagree on resolved edges; an
      independent OpenCode-built oracle gives 14,478 / 0, its earlier gaps
      traced to its own scorer and module coverage.
    - ContextBench, 16 Java rows: routed coverage 0.21 -> 0.76. Identity-only
      successor baselines baseline-v15 and typescript-v12 for the derivation
      id change.
    - docs/java.md documents semantics and limits; docs/phase-6/java-v1 and
      java-v1-opencode hold the evidence. Wheel and sdist smokes cover the
      java fixture.
    - Verified on the exact staged tree: ruff, mypy --strict (70 files),
      pytest 403 passed, 7 skipped.
    
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M669VCEMGTKK2SDDCR99RQ53

# baseline-v15: `java` component identity amendment

The derivation components gain `java` (`oxide-java-v1`) and `java-parser`
(`tree-sitter-java=0.23.5`), and `FACTS_FORMAT` gains `oxide-java-facts-v1`, for the Java
language slice ([../../java.md](../../java.md), evidence in
[../java-v1/README.md](../java-v1/README.md)). The derivation id hashes every component
version, so every index's id changes. The pinned corpora hold no Java, and the Python,
TypeScript, JavaScript, Go and Rust slices and their facts encodings are unchanged.

## Measured against baseline-v14

Same tasks, gold audit, scorer, budgets, corpora and tolerance.

| File | Difference from v14 |
| --- | --- |
| `metrics.json` | byte-identical |
| `results.json` | 44 differences, all `versions.derivation` (`sha256:d89f…` → `sha256:04c2…`); every task's entries, routed set and payload are identical |
| `manifest.json` | 38 corpus `derivation` ids, `versions.derivation`, `oxide_source`, and the `baseline`/`protocol` labels (set to v15 by hand, as in v14) |

This is an identity amendment, not a quality change. `test_output_is_compatible`
reported only the derivation change before the freeze.

Command: `uv run --locked python tests/python/contextbench.py run --out docs/phase-6/baseline-v15`
(run once before the `BASELINE` switch).

"""The frozen Rust Phase 3/4 baselines as read-only oracles (docs/phase-3, docs/phase-4).

Retrieval and routing are expected to reproduce the Rust results exactly on the
fixture. Context packing changed format (``oxide-payload-v3``), so only its
quality floor is compared, never payload bytes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest
from conftest import FIXTURE, REPO

import oxide
from oxide.core import retrieval, routing

BASELINE = json.loads((REPO / "docs/phase-3/baseline-v1/results.json").read_text())


def rust(key: str) -> str:
    """The Rust baseline's entity display: plain paths for files and symbols."""
    return key.split(":", 1)[1] if key.startswith(("file:", "symbol:")) else key


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def repo(tmp_path_factory: pytest.TempPathFactory) -> Iterator[oxide.Repository]:
    data = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("baseline-data")
    with oxide.open_repository(FIXTURE, data_dir=data) as repository:
        repository.index()
        yield repository


@pytest.mark.parametrize("task", BASELINE, ids=[t["task"] for t in BASELINE])
def test_entry_points_and_routes_reproduce_phase3(
    repo: oxide.Repository, fts: Path, task: dict[str, Any]
) -> None:
    run = task["runs"]["lexical+structural"]
    view = repo._view()
    hints = retrieval.Hints(symbols=tuple(task["symbol_hints"]))
    found = retrieval.retrieve(view, task["text"], hints)
    mine = [(rust(e.key), e.rank, bool(e.seeds)) for e in found.entries]
    frozen = [
        (e["entity"], e["lexical"][0][0] if e["lexical"] else None, bool(e["seeds"]))
        for e in run["candidate_set"]["entries"]
    ]
    assert mine == frozen
    scores = [e["lexical"][0][1] if e["lexical"] else None for e in run["candidate_set"]["entries"]]
    assert [e.score for e in found.entries] == pytest.approx(scores, rel=1e-12)
    route = routing.route(view, [e.key for e in found.entries])
    assert sorted((rust(c.key), c.depth) for c in route.candidates) == sorted(
        (c["entity"], c["depth"]) for c in run["route"]["candidates"]
    )


def test_context_quality_floor_matches_phase4(repo: oxide.Repository, fts: Path) -> None:
    """Phase 4 config B packed all 9 gold symbols whole at 1,024 units; at 256 units most
    gold fit only as a header (Rust: 0.071 recall)."""
    recall: dict[int, list[float]] = {256: [], 1024: []}
    for task in BASELINE:
        gold = {f"symbol:{g['entity']}" for g in task["gold"]}
        for budget, values in recall.items():
            bundle = repo.build_context(task["text"], budget, symbols=task["symbol_hints"])
            assert bundle.used <= budget
            whole = {e.key for item in bundle.items for e in item.entities if e.complete}
            values.append(len(gold & whole) / len(gold))
    assert sum(recall[1024]) / len(recall[1024]) == 1.0
    assert sum(recall[256]) / len(recall[256]) < 1.0

"""TreeRouter baseline (SPEC § TreeRouter): level-synchronous BFS over TreeIndex projection 1.

Projection 1 is physical containment (repository > module/file > symbol > symbol);
every other relation is a typed cross-edge. Layer 0 is the entry points, or the root
region when there are none (root fallback). An explored region expands to its
physical children, its containing scope (never the repository root), then both ends
of the followed cross-edges, each in domain order, deduplicated. Every bound fires
visibly. Without a decision provider nothing is pruned, which is the Rust
``oxide-router-bfs-v1`` behavior with no judge.

Adjacency for a whole layer is one store read, so store round trips scale with depth,
not with the number of regions.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from oxide.storage.ladybug import Adjacent, View

ROUTER_VERSION = "oxide-router-bfs-v2"
MAX_REGIONS = 64
MAX_DEPTH = 2
MAX_FANOUT = 16
MAX_EDGES = 2048
FOLLOW = ("calls", "references", "imports", "tested_by", "contains_logical")


def follows(kind: str, heuristic: bool) -> bool:
    """Cross-edges the router walks: ``tested_by`` is its one heuristic kind; heuristic
    calls and references (Python receiver dispatch) are not followed (graph-v2)."""
    return kind in FOLLOW and (kind == "tested_by" or not heuristic)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Routed:
    key: str
    depth: int
    origins: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Route:

"""Go slice conformance (docs/go.md): identity, kinds, provenance, package and module
resolution, tests, cached facts and persisted incremental/full-rebuild equality."""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path

from conftest import REPO, write
from test_incremental import BAD, _paths, _replace, apply, dump
from test_typescript import derived, resolved

import oxide
from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import Derived, derive, dialect, validate
from oxide.core.languages import go, python

FIXTURE = REPO / "fixtures/go_repo"
MOD = "module example.com/m\n\ngo 1.22\n"


def unresolved(result: Derived, kind: str, source: str) -> set[str | None]:
    return {
        e.name
        for e in result.edges
        if e.kind == kind and e.source == source and e.resolution == "unresolved"
    }


def test_import_facts_are_in_source_order() -> None:
    parsed = go.parse(
        b'package p\nimport ("crypto/subtle"\n"encoding/base64"\n"net/http"\n'
        b'"strconv"\n\n"example.com/internal/bytesconv"\n)\n'
    )
    assert not isinstance(parsed, str)
    assert [item.path for item in parsed.imports] == [
        "crypto/subtle",
        "encoding/base64",
        "net/http",
        "strconv",
        "example.com/internal/bytesconv",
    ]


def test_fixture_entities_kinds_and_provenance() -> None:
    found = derived(FIXTURE)
    files = {f.path: f for f in found.files}
    assert all(
        f.language == "go" and f.coverage == "complete"
        for f in found.files
        if f.path.endswith(".go")
    )
    assert files["go.mod"].coverage == "unsupported"
    entities = {e.key: e for e in found.entities}
    kinds = {k: e.kind for k, e in entities.items() if e.category == "symbol"}
    assert kinds["symbol:store/store.go#Store"] == "struct"
    assert kinds["symbol:store/store.go#Backend"] == "interface"
    assert kinds["symbol:store/store.go#Backend.Get"] == "method"
    assert kinds["symbol:store/store.go#Key"] == "type"
    assert kinds["symbol:store/store.go#Store.Get"] == "method"
    assert kinds["symbol:store/config.go#ModeRead"] == "constant"
    assert kinds["symbol:store/config.go#ErrClosed"] == "variable"
    assert kinds["symbol:internal/util/util.go#Map"] == "function"
    # Equal segments take source-order ordinals; a method's segment is Receiver.Name.
    assert kinds["symbol:store/path_windows.go#init~1"] == "function"
    assert entities["symbol:store/store.go#Store.Get"].name == "Get"
    assert entities["symbol:store/store_test.go#TestGet"].test
    assert entities["symbol:store/api_test.go#TestOpen"].test
    assert not entities["symbol:store/api_test.go#Testable"].test
    assert not entities["symbol:store/store_test.go#helper"].test
    modules = {e.key: e.name for e in found.entities if e.category == "module"}
    assert modules == {
        "module:go:cart/cart": "example.com/shop/cart",
        "module:go:cmd/shop/main": "example.com/shop/cmd/shop",
        "module:go:internal/util/util": "example.com/shop/internal/util",
        "module:go:store/store": "example.com/shop/store",
        "module:go:store/store_test": "example.com/shop/store_test",
        "module:go:tools/tools": "example.com/shop/tools",
    }

"""C language slice: tree-sitter syntax facts (docs/c.md); resolution is in ``c_resolve``.

Symbols are file-level declarations, all with the file as physical parent: function
definitions and prototypes, tagged struct/union/enum definitions, typedefs, variables
and macros, including those in every branch of a preprocessor conditional. The
preprocessor never runs and macro bodies stay opaque text. One compiled query collects

_IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*")


def _sound(parsed: Parsed, size: int) -> bool:
    """What ``parse`` guarantees: in-bounds spans, string texts, a file scope then
    symbol scopes, and identifier names, so identities stay unique."""

    def span(a: Any, b: Any) -> bool:
        return type(a) is int and type(b) is int and 0 <= a <= b <= size

    def texts(*values: Any) -> bool:
        return all(type(v) is str for v in values)

    scopes = parsed.scopes
    if not scopes or scopes[0].decl is not None:
        return False
    for k, s in enumerate(scopes):
        d, uses = s.decl, (*s.calls, *s.refs)
        if k and not (
            d is not None
            and d.kind in KINDS
            and type(d.name) is str
            and _IDENTIFIER.fullmatch(d.name) is not None
            and span(d.start, d.end)
            and texts(d.signature)
            and type(d.static) is bool
            and type(d.defines) is bool
        ):
            return False
        if not (
            all(span(u.start, u.end) for u in uses) and texts(*s.bound, *(u.name for u in uses))
        ):
            return False
    return texts(*parsed.diagnostics) and all(
        texts(i.path) and type(i.system) is bool and span(i.start, i.end)
        for i in parsed.includes
    )

"""GCC call-graph oracle for the C slice's call edges (docs/c.md, ../README.md).

Compiles every ``.c`` file under ``SRC`` with ``gcc -fcallgraph-info`` (each
translation unit as the build would) and reads each real call: its site
(file:line:byte column), the callee name, and the callee's file when it is static.
Every oxide ``calls`` edge whose evidence starts at such a site is judged: resolved
edges agree when the target is a function definition of that name in the file that
defines it (the static's own file, else the one file defining it externally).
Macro calls are expanded by GCC, so they have no site and are counted, not judged.

usage: uv run python docs/phase-6/c-v1/oracle/oracle.py ROOT SRC OUT.json [CFLAGS...]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive

_EDGE = re.compile(r'edge: \{ sourcename: "[^"]*" targetname: "([^"]*)" label: "([^"]*)" \}')
_NODE = re.compile(r'node: \{ title: "([^"]*)" label: "[^\\"]*\\n([^"]*?):\d+:\d+')


def main(root: Path, src: Path, out: Path, flags: list[str]) -> None:
    calls: dict[tuple[str, int, int], tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
    defined: dict[str, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)  # external name -> files
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        for unit in sorted(src.glob("*.c")):
            ci = Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.ci"
            cmd = ["gcc", "-c", "-O0", "-fcallgraph-info", "-fdiagnostics-column-unit=byte"]
            cmd += [*flags, str(unit.resolve()), "-o", str(Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.o")]
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, cwd=tmp)
            text = ci.read_text()
            for title, where in _NODE.findall(text):
                if ":" not in title:  # an external definition of this unit
                    if Path(where).resolve() == unit.resolve():
                        defined[title].add(Path(where).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix())
            for target, label in _EDGE.findall(text):
                path, line, col = label.rsplit(":", 2)
                site = (Path(path).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix(), int(line), int(col))
                static, _, name = target.rpartition(":")
                owner = Path(static).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix() if static else None
                calls[site] = (name, owner)
    derived = derive(capture(root), "oracle")
    data = {f.path: f.data for f in capture(root).files}
    entities = {e.key: e for e in derived.entities}
    tally: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    disagreements = []
    for edge in derived.edges:
        if edge.kind != "calls" or edge.evidence is None or not edge.evidence.path.endswith(".c"):
            continue
        ev = edge.evidence
        before = data[ev.path][: ev.start]
        site = (ev.path, before.count(b"\n") + 1, ev.start - (before.rfind(b"\n") + 1) + 1)
        targets = [entities[t] for t in edge.targets]
        if site not in calls:
            macro = targets and all(t.kind == "macro" for t in targets)
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, no gcc call{' (macro)' if macro else ''}"] += 1
            continue
        name, owner = calls[site]
        files = {owner} if owner else defined.get(name, set())
        if edge.resolution != "resolved":
            local = len(files) == 1
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, gcc {'resolved' if local else 'external'}"] += 1
            continue
        (target,) = targets
        assert target.source is not None
        good = target.kind == "function" and target.name == name and {target.source.path} == files
        tally["resolved, agree" if good else "resolved, disagree"] += 1
        if not good:
            disagreements.append({"site": site, "oxide": target.key, "gcc": [name, sorted(files)]})
    report = {"gcc_calls": len(calls), "tally": dict(sorted(tally.items()))}
    out.write_text(json.dumps({**report, "disagreements": disagreements}, indent=1) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4:])

"""GCC call-graph oracle for the C slice's call edges (docs/c.md, ../README.md).

Compiles every ``.c`` file under ``SRC`` with ``gcc -fcallgraph-info`` (each
translation unit as the build would) and reads each real call: its site
(file:line:byte column), the callee name, and the callee's file when it is static.
Every oxide ``calls`` edge whose evidence starts at such a site is judged: resolved
edges agree when the target is a function definition of that name in the file that
defines it (the static's own file, else the one file defining it externally).
Macro calls are expanded by GCC, so they have no site and are counted, not judged.

usage: uv run python docs/phase-6/c-v1/oracle/oracle.py ROOT SRC OUT.json [CFLAGS...]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive

_EDGE = re.compile(r'edge: \{ sourcename: "[^"]*" targetname: "([^"]*)" label: "([^"]*)" \}')
_NODE = re.compile(r'node: \{ title: "([^"]*)" label: "[^\\"]*\\n([^"]*?):\d+:\d+')


def main(root: Path, src: Path, out: Path, flags: list[str]) -> None:
    calls: dict[tuple[str, int, int], tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
    defined: dict[str, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)  # external name -> files
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        for unit in sorted(src.glob("*.c")):
            ci = Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.ci"
            cmd = ["gcc", "-c", "-O0", "-fcallgraph-info", "-fdiagnostics-column-unit=byte"]
            cmd += [*flags, str(unit.resolve()), "-o", str(Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.o")]
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, cwd=tmp)
            text = ci.read_text()
            for title, where in _NODE.findall(text):
                if ":" not in title:  # an external definition of this unit
                    if Path(where).resolve() == unit.resolve():
                        defined[title].add(Path(where).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix())
            for target, label in _EDGE.findall(text):
                path, line, col = label.rsplit(":", 2)
                site = (Path(path).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix(), int(line), int(col))
                static, _, name = target.rpartition(":")
                owner = Path(static).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix() if static else None
                calls[site] = (name, owner)
    derived = derive(capture(root), "oracle")
    data = {f.path: f.data for f in capture(root).files}
    entities = {e.key: e for e in derived.entities}
    tally: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    disagreements = []
    for edge in derived.edges:
        if edge.kind != "calls" or edge.evidence is None or not edge.evidence.path.endswith(".c"):
            continue
        ev = edge.evidence
        before = data[ev.path][: ev.start]
        site = (ev.path, before.count(b"\n") + 1, ev.start - (before.rfind(b"\n") + 1) + 1)
        targets = [entities[t] for t in edge.targets]
        if site not in calls:
            macro = targets and all(t.kind == "macro" for t in targets)
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, no gcc call{' (macro)' if macro else ''}"] += 1
            continue
        name, owner = calls[site]
        files = {owner} if owner else defined.get(name, set())
        if edge.resolution != "resolved":
            local = len(files) == 1
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, gcc {'resolved' if local else 'external'}"] += 1
            continue
        (target,) = targets
        assert target.source is not None
        good = target.kind == "function" and target.name == name and {target.source.path} == files
        tally["resolved, agree" if good else "resolved, disagree"] += 1
        if not good:
            disagreements.append({"site": site, "oxide": target.key, "gcc": [name, sorted(files)]})
    report = {"gcc_calls": len(calls), "tally": dict(sorted(tally.items()))}
    out.write_text(json.dumps({**report, "disagreements": disagreements}, indent=1) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4:])

"""GCC call-graph oracle for the C slice's call edges (docs/c.md, ../README.md).

Compiles every ``.c`` file under ``SRC`` with ``gcc -fcallgraph-info`` (each
translation unit as the build would) and reads each real call: its site
(file:line:byte column), the callee name, and the callee's file when it is static.
Every oxide ``calls`` edge whose evidence starts at such a site is judged: resolved
edges agree when the target is a function definition of that name in the file that
defines it (the static's own file, else the one file defining it externally).
Macro calls are expanded by GCC, so they have no site and are counted, not judged.

usage: uv run python docs/phase-6/c-v1/oracle/oracle.py ROOT SRC OUT.json [CFLAGS...]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive

_EDGE = re.compile(r'edge: \{ sourcename: "[^"]*" targetname: "([^"]*)" label: "([^"]*)" \}')
_NODE = re.compile(r'node: \{ title: "([^"]*)" label: "[^\\"]*\\n([^"]*?):\d+:\d+')


def main(root: Path, src: Path, out: Path, flags: list[str]) -> None:
    calls: dict[tuple[str, int, int], tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
    defined: dict[str, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)  # external name -> files
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        for unit in sorted(src.glob("*.c")):
            ci = Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.ci"
            cmd = ["gcc", "-c", "-O0", "-fcallgraph-info", "-fdiagnostics-column-unit=byte"]
            cmd += [*flags, str(unit.resolve()), "-o", str(Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.o")]
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, cwd=tmp)
            text = ci.read_text()
            for title, where in _NODE.findall(text):
                if ":" not in title:  # an external definition of this unit
                    if Path(where).resolve() == unit.resolve():
                        defined[title].add(Path(where).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix())
            for target, label in _EDGE.findall(text):
                path, line, col = label.rsplit(":", 2)
                site = (Path(path).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix(), int(line), int(col))
                static, _, name = target.rpartition(":")
                owner = Path(static).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix() if static else None
                calls[site] = (name, owner)
    derived = derive(capture(root), "oracle")
    data = {f.path: f.data for f in capture(root).files}
    entities = {e.key: e for e in derived.entities}
    tally: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    disagreements = []
    for edge in derived.edges:
        if edge.kind != "calls" or edge.evidence is None or not edge.evidence.path.endswith(".c"):
            continue
        ev = edge.evidence
        before = data[ev.path][: ev.start]
        site = (ev.path, before.count(b"\n") + 1, ev.start - (before.rfind(b"\n") + 1) + 1)
        targets = [entities[t] for t in edge.targets]
        if site not in calls:
            macro = targets and all(t.kind == "macro" for t in targets)
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, no gcc call{' (macro)' if macro else ''}"] += 1
            continue
        name, owner = calls[site]
        files = {owner} if owner else defined.get(name, set())
        if edge.resolution != "resolved":
            local = len(files) == 1
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, gcc {'resolved' if local else 'external'}"] += 1
            continue
        (target,) = targets
        assert target.source is not None
        good = target.kind == "function" and target.name == name and {target.source.path} == files
        tally["resolved, agree" if good else "resolved, disagree"] += 1
        if not good:
            disagreements.append({"site": site, "oxide": target.key, "gcc": [name, sorted(files)]})
    report = {"gcc_calls": len(calls), "tally": dict(sorted(tally.items()))}
    out.write_text(json.dumps({**report, "disagreements": disagreements}, indent=1) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4:])

    for edge in derived.edges:
        if edge.kind != "calls" or edge.evidence is None or not edge.evidence.path.endswith(".c"):
            continue
        ev = edge.evidence
        before = data[ev.path][: ev.start]
        site = (ev.path, before.count(b"\n") + 1, ev.start - (before.rfind(b"\n") + 1) + 1)
        targets = [entities[t] for t in edge.targets]
        if targets and all(t.kind == "macro" for t in targets):  # gcc sees the expansion
            tally[f"{edge.resolution} to a macro, not judged"] += 1
            continue
        if site not in calls:  # inside a macro argument gcc may report another column
            line = [c for at, c in calls.items() if at[:2] == site[:2] and c[0] == edge.name]
            line = line or [c for at, c in calls.items() if at[:2] == site[:2]]
            names = {entities[t].name for t in edge.targets}
            same = [c for c in line if c[0] in names]
            if len(same) == 1:
                site = next(at for at, c in calls.items() if at[:2] == site[:2] and c == same[0])
        if site not in calls:
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, no gcc call"] += 1
            if edge.resolution == "resolved":
                unseen.append({"site": site, "oxide": edge.targets[0]})
            continue
        name, owner = calls[site]
        files = {owner} if owner else defined.get(name, set())
        if edge.resolution != "resolved":
            local = len(files) == 1
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, gcc {'resolved' if local else 'external'}"] += 1
            continue
        (target,) = targets
        assert target.source is not None
        good = target.kind == "function" and target.name == name and {target.source.path} == files
        tally["resolved, agree" if good else "resolved, disagree"] += 1

"""GCC call-graph oracle for the C slice's call edges (docs/c.md, ../README.md).

Compiles every ``.c`` file under ``SRC`` with ``gcc -fcallgraph-info`` (each
translation unit as the build would) and reads each real call: its site
(file:line:byte column), the callee name, and the callee's file when it is static.
Every oxide ``calls`` edge whose evidence starts at such a site is judged: resolved
edges agree when the target is a function definition of that name in the file that
defines it (the static's own file, else the one file defining it externally).
GCC reports a macro's expansion at its use site, so edges to macros are counted, not
judged.

usage: uv run python docs/phase-6/c-v1/oracle/oracle.py ROOT SRC OUT.json [CFLAGS...]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive

_EDGE = re.compile(r'edge: \{ sourcename: "[^"]*" targetname: "([^"]*)" label: "([^"]*)" \}')
_NODE = re.compile(r'node: \{ title: "([^"]*)" label: "[^\\"]*\\n([^"]*?):\d+:\d+')


def main(root: Path, src: Path, out: Path, flags: list[str]) -> None:
    calls: dict[tuple[str, int, int], tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
    defined: dict[str, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)  # external name -> files
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        for unit in sorted(src.glob("*.c")):
            ci = Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.ci"
            cmd = ["gcc", "-c", "-O0", "-fcallgraph-info", "-fdiagnostics-column-unit=byte"]
            cmd += [*flags, str(unit.resolve()), "-o", str(Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.o")]
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, cwd=tmp)
            text = ci.read_text()
            for title, where in _NODE.findall(text):
                if ":" not in title:  # an external definition of this unit
                    if Path(where).resolve() == unit.resolve():
                        defined[title].add(Path(where).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix())
            for target, label in _EDGE.findall(text):
                path, line, col = label.rsplit(":", 2)
                site = (Path(path).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix(), int(line), int(col))
                static, _, name = target.rpartition(":")
                owner = Path(static).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix() if static else None
                calls[site] = (name, owner)
    derived = derive(capture(root), "oracle")
    data = {f.path: f.data for f in capture(root).files}
    entities = {e.key: e for e in derived.entities}
    tally: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    disagreements: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    unseen: list[dict[str, object]] = []  # resolved, but no call in this build
    for edge in derived.edges:
        if edge.kind != "calls" or edge.evidence is None or not edge.evidence.path.endswith(".c"):
            continue
        ev = edge.evidence
        before = data[ev.path][: ev.start]
        site = (ev.path, before.count(b"\n") + 1, ev.start - (before.rfind(b"\n") + 1) + 1)
        targets = [entities[t] for t in edge.targets]
        if targets and all(t.kind == "macro" for t in targets):  # gcc sees the expansion
            tally[f"{edge.resolution} to a macro, not judged"] += 1
            continue
        if site not in calls:  # inside a macro argument gcc may report another column
            line = [c for at, c in calls.items() if at[:2] == site[:2] and c[0] == edge.name]
            line = line or [c for at, c in calls.items() if at[:2] == site[:2]]

"""GCC call-graph oracle for the C slice's call edges (docs/c.md, ../README.md).

Compiles every ``.c`` file under ``SRC`` with ``gcc -fcallgraph-info`` (each
translation unit as the build would) and reads each real call: its site
(file:line:byte column), the callee name, and the callee's file when it is static.
Every oxide ``calls`` edge whose evidence starts at such a site is judged: resolved
edges agree when the target is a function definition of that name in the file that
defines it (the static's own file, else the one file defining it externally).
GCC reports a macro's expansion at its use site, so edges to macros are counted, not
judged.

usage: uv run python docs/phase-6/c-v1/oracle/oracle.py ROOT SRC OUT.json [CFLAGS...]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive

_EDGE = re.compile(r'edge: \{ sourcename: "[^"]*" targetname: "([^"]*)" label: "([^"]*)" \}')
_NODE = re.compile(r'node: \{ title: "([^"]*)" label: "[^\\"]*\\n([^"]*?):\d+:\d+')


def main(root: Path, src: Path, out: Path, flags: list[str]) -> None:
    calls: dict[tuple[str, int, int], tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
    defined: dict[str, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)  # external name -> files
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        for unit in sorted(src.glob("*.c")):
            ci = Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.ci"
            cmd = ["gcc", "-c", "-O0", "-fcallgraph-info", "-fdiagnostics-column-unit=byte"]
            cmd += [*flags, str(unit.resolve()), "-o", str(Path(tmp) / f"{unit.stem}.o")]
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, cwd=tmp)
            text = ci.read_text()
            for title, where in _NODE.findall(text):
                if ":" not in title:  # an external definition of this unit
                    if Path(where).resolve() == unit.resolve():
                        defined[title].add(Path(where).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix())
            for target, label in _EDGE.findall(text):
                path, line, col = label.rsplit(":", 2)
                site = (Path(path).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix(), int(line), int(col))
                static, _, name = target.rpartition(":")
                owner = Path(static).resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix() if static else None
                calls[site] = (name, owner)
    derived = derive(capture(root), "oracle")
    data = {f.path: f.data for f in capture(root).files}
    entities = {e.key: e for e in derived.entities}
    tally: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    disagreements: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    unseen: list[dict[str, object]] = []  # resolved, but no call in this build
    for edge in derived.edges:
        if edge.kind != "calls" or edge.evidence is None or not edge.evidence.path.endswith(".c"):
            continue
        ev = edge.evidence
        before = data[ev.path][: ev.start]
        site = (ev.path, before.count(b"\n") + 1, ev.start - (before.rfind(b"\n") + 1) + 1)
        targets = [entities[t] for t in edge.targets]
        if targets and all(t.kind == "macro" for t in targets):  # gcc sees the expansion
            tally[f"{edge.resolution} to a macro, not judged"] += 1
            continue
        if site not in calls:  # in a macro argument gcc reports another column: same line
            names = {t.name for t in targets}
            same = [at for at in lines.get(site[:2], []) if calls[at][0] in names]
            site = same[0] if len(same) == 1 else site
        if site not in calls:
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, no gcc call"] += 1
            if edge.resolution == "resolved":
                unseen.append({"site": site, "oxide": edge.targets[0]})
            continue
        name, owner = calls[site]
        files = {owner} if owner else defined.get(name, set())
        if edge.resolution != "resolved":
            local = len(files) == 1
            tally[f"{edge.resolution}, gcc {'resolved' if local else 'external'}"] += 1
            continue
        (target,) = targets
        assert target.source is not None
        good = target.kind == "function" and target.name == name and {target.source.path} == files
        tally["resolved, agree" if good else "resolved, disagree"] += 1
        if not good:
            disagreements.append({"site": site, "oxide": target.key, "gcc": [name, sorted(files)]})
    report = {"gcc_calls": len(calls), "tally": dict(sorted(tally.items()))}
    full = {**report, "disagreements": disagreements, "unseen": unseen}
    out.write_text(json.dumps(full, indent=1) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve(), Path(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4:])

"""C slice conformance (docs/c.md): identity, kinds, provenance, include and linkage
resolution, macro recovery, cached facts and persisted incremental/full-rebuild equality."""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path

from conftest import REPO, write
from test_go import unresolved
from test_incremental import BAD, _paths, _replace, apply, dump
from test_typescript import derived, resolved

import oxide
from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive, dialect, validate
from oxide.core.languages import c, python

FIXTURE = REPO / "fixtures/c_repo"
HEADER = "symbol:include/shop/store.h"


def test_fixture_entities_kinds_and_provenance() -> None:
    found = derived(FIXTURE)
    files = {f.path: f for f in found.files}
    assert all(
        f.language == "c" and f.coverage == "complete"
        for f in found.files
        if f.path.endswith((".c", ".h"))
    )
    assert files["Makefile"].coverage == "unsupported"
    entities = {e.key: e for e in found.entities}
    kinds = {k: e.kind for k, e in entities.items() if e.category == "symbol"}
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#STORE_EMPTY"] == "macro"
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#Key"] == "type"
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#Entry"] == "struct"
    # A tag and its same-named typedef: the tag, then the declaration holding it.
    assert (kinds[f"{HEADER}#Store"], kinds[f"{HEADER}#Store~1"]) == ("struct", "type")
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#Mode"] == "enum"
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#store_default_limit"] == "variable"
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#store_get"] == "function"  # a prototype
    assert kinds["symbol:src/store.c#store_get"] == "function"  # its definition
    assert kinds["symbol:src/cart.c#hash_key"] == "function"
    assert not any(e.test for e in found.entities)
    assert not any(e.category == "module" for e in found.entities)
    data = {f.path: f.data for f in capture(FIXTURE).files}
    for key, text in [
        (f"{HEADER}#STORE_MAX", "#define STORE_MAX 64\n"),
        (f"{HEADER}#Key", "typedef const char *Key;"),
        (f"{HEADER}#store_get", "const char *store_get(Store *s, Key key);"),
        (f"{HEADER}#Mode", "enum Mode { MODE_READ = 1, MODE_WRITE = 2 }"),
    ]:
        source = entities[key].source
        assert source is not None and source.digest == files[source.path].digest
        assert data[source.path][source.start : source.end].decode() == text
    assert entities["symbol:src/store.c#store_open"].signature == "Store *store_open(enum Mode mode)"
    assert entities[f"{HEADER}#Store~1"].signature == "typedef struct Store Store;"
    assert entities[f"{HEADER}#Store"].signature == "struct Store"


def test_fixture_relations() -> None:
    found = derived(FIXTURE)
    # Beside the including file, relative, or by a unique path suffix (``-Iinclude``).
    assert resolved(found, "imports", "file:src/cart.c") == {"file:src/cart.h"}
    assert resolved(found, "imports", "file:src/cart.h") == {"file:include/shop/store.h"}
    assert resolved(found, "imports", "file:src/store.c") == {"file:include/shop/store.h"}
    assert unresolved(found, "imports", "file:src/store.c") == {"stdlib.h", "string.h"}
    # Linkage: a file's own static wins; an external definition anywhere otherwise.
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_add") == {"symbol:src/cart.c#hash_key"}
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/store.c#store_get") == {
        "symbol:src/store.c#hash_key",
        f"{HEADER}#STORE_EMPTY",  # a macro call
        f"{HEADER}#store_size",  # a static inline in an included header
    }
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/main.c#main") == {
        "symbol:src/store.c#store_open",
        "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_add",
        "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_first",
    }
    # A local function pointer is opaque; the C library stays unresolved.
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_first") == {
        "symbol:src/store.c#store_must_get"
    }
    assert unresolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_first") == {"get"}
    assert unresolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/main.c#main") == {"printf"}
    # Prototypes reference their definitions; types and tags resolve through includes.
    assert resolved(found, "references", f"{HEADER}#store_get") == {
        "symbol:src/store.c#store_get",
        f"{HEADER}#Store~1",
        f"{HEADER}#Key",
    }
    assert resolved(found, "references", "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_add") == {
        "symbol:src/cart.h#Cart",
        f"{HEADER}#Key",
    }
    assert resolved(found, "references", f"{HEADER}#Store") == {f"{HEADER}#Entry"}
    # Conditional compilation is not evaluated: platform files are not chosen between.
    ambiguous = {(e.source, e.targets) for e in found.edges if e.resolution == "ambiguous"}
    platforms = ("symbol:src/path_posix.c#platform_path", "symbol:src/path_windows.c#platform_path")
    assert ambiguous == {("symbol:src/main.c#main", platforms), (f"{HEADER}#platform_path", platforms)}


def test_search_and_context(tmp_path: Path, fts: Path) -> None:
    with oxide.open_repository(FIXTURE, data_dir=tmp_path / "data") as repo:
        repo.index()
        result = repo.search("must get store entries", symbols=["store_must_get"])
        assert result.entries[0].entity.key in {
            "symbol:src/store.c#store_must_get",
            f"{HEADER}#store_must_get",
        }
        bundle = repo.build_context("open the store", symbols=["store_open"], budget=1024)
        assert 0 < bundle.used <= 1024
        assert "Store *store_open(enum Mode mode)" in bundle.payload


def test_scoping_and_linkage_are_conservative(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    found = derived(
        write(
            tmp_path,
            {
                "a.h": "#define twice(x) ((x) * 2)\nstatic int shared(void) { return 1; }\n"
                "typedef int T;\n",
                "a.c": '#include "a.h"\nint f(void) { return 1; }\nint twice(int x);\n'
                "int g(int f) { return f(); }\n"
                "int h(void) { int (*shared)(void) = 0; return shared(); }\n"
                "int k(void) { typedef long T; T x = 0; struct S { int a; } s; struct S *p;"
                " return twice(f()) + shared(); }\n",
                "b.c": "static int hidden(void) { return 0; }\nint f(void) { return 2; }\n",
                "c.c": "int c(void) { return hidden() + shared() + f(); }\n",
            },
        )
    )
    assert not resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:a.c#g")  # a parameter named f
    assert not resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:a.c#h")  # a local named shared
    # Macros win over a same-named function; a visible definition over one elsewhere.
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:a.c#k") == {
        "symbol:a.h#twice",
        "symbol:a.c#f",
        "symbol:a.h#shared",
    }
    assert not resolved(found, "references", "symbol:a.c#k")  # local typedef and tag
    # Another file's static is invisible; externals of other files are ambiguous.
    assert unresolved(found, "calls", "symbol:c.c#c") == {"hidden", "shared"}
    assert {e.targets for e in found.edges if e.source == "symbol:c.c#c" and e.name == "f"} == {
        ("symbol:a.c#f", "symbol:b.c#f")
    }


def test_include_resolution(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    found = derived(
        write(
            tmp_path,
            {
                "lib/stdio.h": "int mine;\n",
                "lib/x/util.h": "int util;\n",
                "one/dup.h": "",
                "two/dup.h": "",
                "src/a.c": '#include <stdio.h>\n#include <x/util.h>\n#include "dup.h"\n'
                '#include "../lib/stdio.h"\n#include "missing.h"\n#include NAME\n',
            },
        )
    )
    imports = {e.evidence.start if e.evidence else -1: e for e in found.edges if e.kind == "imports"}
    edges = [imports[k] for k in sorted(imports)]
    assert [(e.resolution, e.targets) for e in edges] == [
        ("unresolved", ()),  # an angle include without a directory is the system's
        ("resolved", ("file:lib/x/util.h",)),
        ("ambiguous", ("file:one/dup.h", "file:two/dup.h")),
        ("resolved", ("file:lib/stdio.h",)),
        ("unresolved", ()),
    ]
    assert dialect("a/b.h") == dialect("a/b.c") == "c"


def test_macro_annotated_declarations_recover_their_names() -> None:
    parsed = c.parse(
        b"API lua_Integer luaL_len (lua_State *L, int idx) { return 1; }\n"
        b"API int lua_gettop (lua_State *L) { return 0; }\n"
        b"API int (lua_settop) (lua_State *L, int idx);\n"
        b"#define fastget(t,slot) \\\n  (!t  /* no table */  \\\n   ? (slot = 0)  \\\n"
        b"   : (slot = get(t)))  /* done */\n"
        b'const char *s = "/* text */"; char q = \'"\'; /* a\n comment */ int after;\n'
    )
    assert not isinstance(parsed, str)
    decls = [(s.decl.kind, s.decl.name) for s in parsed.scopes[1:] if s.decl]
    # A keyword is never a name: the parenthesized prototype is not a symbol.
    assert decls == [
        ("function", "luaL_len"),
        ("function", "lua_gettop"),
        ("macro", "fastget"),
        ("variable", "s"),
        ("variable", "q"),
        ("variable", "after"),
    ]
    macro = next(s.decl for s in parsed.scopes[1:] if s.decl and s.decl.kind == "macro")
    assert macro.signature == "#define fastget(t,slot)"


def test_identity_is_local_and_deterministic(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    files = {"a.c": "int f(void);\nint f(void) { return 0; }\n#ifdef X\nint g;\n#else\nint g;\n#endif\n"}
    first = derived(write(tmp_path / "one", files))
    second = derived(write(tmp_path / "two", {**files, "b.c": "int f(void) { return 1; }\n"}))
    keys = {e.key for e in first.entities}
    assert {"symbol:a.c#f", "symbol:a.c#f~1", "symbol:a.c#g", "symbol:a.c#g~1"} <= keys
    assert keys <= {e.key for e in second.entities}
    assert derived(tmp_path / "one") == first


def test_coverage_cache_validation_and_limits(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    root = write(
        tmp_path,
        {
            "ok.c": "int ok(void) { return 0; }\n",
            "broken.c": "int broken( {\n\treturn\n}\n\nint after(void) { return 1; }\n",
            "latin.h": b"// \xff\n",
        },
    )
    full = derived(root)
    files = {f.path: f for f in full.files}
    assert files["broken.c"].coverage == "partial" and files["broken.c"].diagnostics
    assert files["latin.h"].coverage == "unsupported"
    assert "symbol:broken.c#after" in {e.key for e in full.entities}
    assert set(full.facts) == {"c"}
    for f in capture(root).files:
        parsed = c.parse(f.data)
        if not isinstance(parsed, str):
            assert c.decode(json.loads(json.dumps(c.encode(parsed))), len(f.data)) == parsed
    assert derive(capture(root), "test-repo", full.facts).reused == 2
    cached = copy.deepcopy(full.facts)
    for key in cached["c"]:
        cached["c"][key] = ["damaged"]
    assert derive(capture(root), "test-repo", cached) == full
    deep = ("int x = " + "(" * 70000 + "1" + ")" * 70000 + ";\n").encode()
    assert c.parse(deep) == python.TOO_DEEP


def test_unsound_cached_facts_are_parsed_never_trusted_or_fatal(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    source = (
        '#include "a.h"\n#define M(x) (x)\ntypedef struct S { int a; } T;\n'
        "static int f(T *t, struct S *s) { return M(g(t->a)); }\nint v, w;\n"
    )
    snapshot = capture(write(tmp_path / "repo", {"p/a.c": source}))
    full = derive(snapshot, "r")
    ((key, good),) = full.facts["c"].items()
    size = len(snapshot.files[0].data)
    rejected = 0
    for at in _paths(good):
        for bad in BAD:
            entry = _replace(good, at, bad)
            try:
                c.decode(entry, size)
            except ValueError:
                rejected += 1
                result = derive(snapshot, "r", {"c": {key: entry}})
                assert result == full and result.reused == 0, (at, bad)
                continue
            # Well-formed facts parse could have produced: they may differ, never fail.
            validate(derive(snapshot, "r", {"c": {key: entry}}))
    assert rejected > len(_paths(good)) * len(BAD) // 2


def test_persisted_incremental_equals_full_rebuild(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    root = write(
        tmp_path / "repo",
        {
            "inc/a.h": "int a(void);\n",
            "a.c": '#include "inc/a.h"\nint a(void) { return 0; }\n',
            "b.c": '#include "a.h"\nint b(void) { return a(); }\n',
        },
    )
    steps: list[dict[str, str | bytes | None]] = [
        {"more.c": "int more(void) { return b(); }\n"},
        {"inc/a.h": None, "a.h": "#define a() 0\n"},  # includes re-resolve, facts reused
        {"a.c": "static int a(void) { return 1; }\n", "more.c": None},
        {"b.c": "typedef int a;\nint b(void) { a x = 0; return x; }\n"},
    ]
    with oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=tmp_path / "incremental") as repo:
        repo.index()
        for i, edits in enumerate(steps):
            apply(root, edits)
            report = repo.index()
            assert report.reused >= 1
            with oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=tmp_path / f"full-{i}") as fresh:
                fresh.index()
                assert dump(repo) == dump(fresh)

def test_scoping_and_linkage_are_conservative(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    found = derived(
        write(
            tmp_path,
            {
                "a.h": "#define twice(x) ((x) * 2)\nstatic int shared(void) { return 1; }\n"
                "typedef int T;\n",
                "a.c": '#include "a.h"\nint f(void) { return 1; }\nint twice(int x);\n'
                "int g(int f) { return f(); }\n"
                "int h(void) { int (*shared)(void) = 0; return shared(); }\n"
                "int k(void) { typedef long T; T x = 0; struct S { int a; } s; struct S *p;"
                " return twice(f()) + shared(); }\n",
                "b.c": "static int hidden(void) { return 0; }\nint f(void) { return 2; }\n",
                "c.c": "int c(void) { return hidden() + shared() + f(); }\n",
            },
        )
    )
    assert not resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:a.c#g")  # a parameter named f
    assert not resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:a.c#h")  # a local named shared
    # Macros win over a same-named function; a visible definition over one elsewhere.
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:a.c#k") == {
        "symbol:a.h#twice",
        "symbol:a.c#f",
        "symbol:a.h#shared",
    }
    assert not resolved(found, "references", "symbol:a.c#k")  # local typedef and tag
    # Another file's static is invisible; externals of other files are ambiguous.
    assert unresolved(found, "calls", "symbol:c.c#c") == {"hidden", "shared"}
    assert {e.targets for e in found.edges if e.source == "symbol:c.c#c" and e.name == "f"} == {
        ("symbol:a.c#f", "symbol:b.c#f")
    }


def test_include_resolution(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    found = derived(
        write(
            tmp_path,
            {
                "lib/stdio.h": "int mine;\n",
                "lib/x/util.h": "int util;\n",
                "one/dup.h": "",
                "two/dup.h": "",
                "src/a.c": '#include <stdio.h>\n#include <x/util.h>\n#include "dup.h"\n'
                '#include "../lib/stdio.h"\n#include "missing.h"\n#include NAME\n',
            },
        )
    )
    imports = {e.evidence.start if e.evidence else -1: e for e in found.edges if e.kind == "imports"}
    edges = [imports[k] for k in sorted(imports)]
    assert [(e.resolution, e.targets) for e in edges] == [
        ("unresolved", ()),  # an angle include without a directory is the system's
        ("resolved", ("file:lib/x/util.h",)),
        ("ambiguous", ("file:one/dup.h", "file:two/dup.h")),
        ("resolved", ("file:lib/stdio.h",)),
        ("unresolved", ()),

def test_macro_annotated_declarations_recover_their_names() -> None:
    parsed = c.parse(
        b"API lua_Integer luaL_len (lua_State *L, int idx) { return 1; }\n"
        b"API int lua_gettop (lua_State *L) { return 0; }\n"
        b"API int (lua_settop) (lua_State *L, int idx);\n"
        b"#define fastget(t,slot) \\\n  (!t  /* no table */  \\\n   ? (slot = 0)  \\\n"
        b"   : (slot = get(t)))  /* done */\n"
        b'const char *s = "/* text */"; char q = \'"\'; /* a\n comment */ int after;\n'
    )
    assert not isinstance(parsed, str)
    decls = [(s.decl.kind, s.decl.name) for s in parsed.scopes[1:] if s.decl]
    # A keyword is never a name: the parenthesized prototype is not a symbol.
    assert decls == [
        ("function", "luaL_len"),
        ("function", "lua_gettop"),
        ("macro", "fastget"),
        ("variable", "s"),
        ("variable", "q"),
        ("variable", "after"),
    ]
    macro = next(s.decl for s in parsed.scopes[1:] if s.decl and s.decl.kind == "macro")
    assert macro.signature == "#define fastget(t,slot)"

def test_unsound_cached_facts_are_parsed_never_trusted_or_fatal(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    source = (
        '#include "a.h"\n#define M(x) (x)\ntypedef struct S { int a; } T;\n'
        "static int f(T *t, struct S *s) { return M(g(t->a)); }\nint v, w;\n"
    )
    snapshot = capture(write(tmp_path / "repo", {"p/a.c": source}))
    full = derive(snapshot, "r")
    ((key, good),) = full.facts["c"].items()
    size = len(snapshot.files[0].data)
    rejected = 0
    for at in _paths(good):
        for bad in BAD:
            entry = _replace(good, at, bad)
            try:
                c.decode(entry, size)
            except ValueError:
                rejected += 1
                result = derive(snapshot, "r", {"c": {key: entry}})
                assert result == full and result.reused == 0, (at, bad)
                continue
            # Well-formed facts parse could have produced: they may differ, never fail.
            validate(derive(snapshot, "r", {"c": {key: entry}}))
    assert rejected > len(_paths(good)) * len(BAD) // 2


def test_persisted_incremental_equals_full_rebuild(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    root = write(
        tmp_path / "repo",
        {
            "inc/a.h": "int a(void);\n",
            "a.c": '#include "inc/a.h"\nint a(void) { return 0; }\n',
            "b.c": '#include "a.h"\nint b(void) { return a(); }\n',
        },
    )
    steps: list[dict[str, str | bytes | None]] = [
        {"more.c": "int more(void) { return b(); }\n"},
        {"inc/a.h": None, "a.h": "#define a() 0\n"},  # includes re-resolve, facts reused
        {"a.c": "static int a(void) { return 1; }\n", "more.c": None},
        {"b.c": "typedef int a;\nint b(void) { a x = 0; return x; }\n"},
    ]
    with oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=tmp_path / "incremental") as repo:
        repo.index()
        for i, edits in enumerate(steps):
            apply(root, edits)
            report = repo.index()
            assert report.reused >= 1
            with oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=tmp_path / f"full-{i}") as fresh:
                fresh.index()
                assert dump(repo) == dump(fresh)

        for f in found.files

    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#Entry"] == "struct"

FIXTURE = REPO / "fixtures/c_repo"
HEADER = "symbol:include/shop/store.h"


def test_fixture_entities_kinds_and_provenance() -> None:
    found = derived(FIXTURE)
    files = {f.path: f for f in found.files}
    assert all(
        f.language == "c" and f.coverage == "complete"
        for f in found.files
        if f.path.endswith((".c", ".h"))
    )
    assert files["Makefile"].coverage == "unsupported"
    entities = {e.key: e for e in found.entities}
    kinds = {k: e.kind for k, e in entities.items() if e.category == "symbol"}
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#STORE_EMPTY"] == "macro"
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#Key"] == "type"
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#Entry"] == "struct"
    # A tag and its same-named typedef: the tag, then the declaration holding it.
    assert (kinds[f"{HEADER}#Store"], kinds[f"{HEADER}#Store~1"]) == ("struct", "type")
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#Mode"] == "enum"
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#store_default_limit"] == "variable"
    assert kinds[f"{HEADER}#store_get"] == "function"  # a prototype
    assert kinds["symbol:src/store.c#store_get"] == "function"  # its definition
    assert kinds["symbol:src/cart.c#hash_key"] == "function"
    assert not any(e.test for e in found.entities)
    assert not any(e.category == "module" for e in found.entities)
    data = {f.path: f.data for f in capture(FIXTURE).files}
    for key, text in [
        (f"{HEADER}#STORE_MAX", "#define STORE_MAX 64\n"),
        (f"{HEADER}#Key", "typedef const char *Key;"),
        (f"{HEADER}#store_get", "const char *store_get(Store *s, Key key);"),
        (f"{HEADER}#Mode", "enum Mode { MODE_READ = 1, MODE_WRITE = 2 }"),
    ]:
        source = entities[key].source
        assert source is not None and source.digest == files[source.path].digest
        assert data[source.path][source.start : source.end].decode() == text
    assert entities["symbol:src/store.c#store_open"].signature == "Store *store_open(enum Mode mode)"
    assert entities[f"{HEADER}#Store~1"].signature == "typedef struct Store Store;"
    assert entities[f"{HEADER}#Store"].signature == "struct Store"


def test_fixture_relations() -> None:
    found = derived(FIXTURE)
    # Beside the including file, relative, or by a unique path suffix (``-Iinclude``).
    assert resolved(found, "imports", "file:src/cart.c") == {"file:src/cart.h"}
    assert resolved(found, "imports", "file:src/cart.h") == {"file:include/shop/store.h"}
    assert resolved(found, "imports", "file:src/store.c") == {"file:include/shop/store.h"}
    assert unresolved(found, "imports", "file:src/store.c") == {"stdlib.h", "string.h"}
    # Linkage: a file's own static wins; an external definition anywhere otherwise.
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_add") == {"symbol:src/cart.c#hash_key"}
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/store.c#store_get") == {
        "symbol:src/store.c#hash_key",
        f"{HEADER}#STORE_EMPTY",  # a macro call
        f"{HEADER}#store_size",  # a static inline in an included header
    }
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/main.c#main") == {
        "symbol:src/store.c#store_open",
        "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_add",
        "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_first",
    }
    # A local function pointer is opaque; the C library stays unresolved.
    assert resolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_first") == {
        "symbol:src/store.c#store_must_get"
    }
    assert unresolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/cart.c#cart_first") == {"get"}
    assert unresolved(found, "calls", "symbol:src/main.c#main") == {"printf"}
    # Prototypes reference their definitions; types and tags resolve through includes.
    assert resolved(found, "references", f"{HEADER}#store_get") == {
        "symbol:src/store.c#store_get",
        f"{HEADER}#Store~1",
        f"{HEADER}#Key",

    ambiguous = {(e.source, e.targets) for e in found.edges if e.resolution == "ambiguous"}
    platforms = ("symbol:src/path_posix.c#platform_path", "symbol:src/path_windows.c#platform_path")

            {

                "typedef int T;\n",
                "a.c": '#include "a.h"\nint f(void) { return 1; }\nint twice(int x);\n'
                "int g(int f) { return f(); }\n"
                "int h(void) { int (*shared)(void) = 0; return shared(); }\n"
                "int k(void) { typedef long T; T x = 0; struct S { int a; } s; struct S *p;"
                " return twice(f()) + shared(); }\n",

    assert unresolved(found, "calls", "symbol:c.c#c") == {"hidden", "shared"}
